chief_complaint: Routine management of type 2 diabetes mellitus and associated metabolic syndrome
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 62-year-old white male with a longstanding history of obesity, type 2 diabetes (diagnosed 2020), essential hypertension, hypertriglyceridemia, metabolic syndrome, anemia, and chronic stress. Over the past three years his care has focused on regular wellness visits, diabetes surveillance (multiple retinal photographs), and hypertension control with lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide. Recent laboratory data are limited; the most recent A1c is 6.7%, suggesting borderline glycemic control. No lipid panel, blood pressure readings, or renal function tests are available. Socially, he works part‑time, has a criminal record, and reports ongoing stress, which may affect adherence and lifestyle modifications.
past_medical_history: Resolved conditions include viral sinusitis (2022), acute viral pharyngitis (2022), colon polyp (2022), prior reports of violence in the environment (2021), previous medication review entries (2017, 2019), full‑time employment (ended 2021), resolved social isolation (2019), and two lacerations of the thigh (2016).

Lisinopril 10 MG Oral Tablet
active_medications.purpose: Hypertension and renal protection in diabetes

social_determinants: Part‑time employment, documented criminal record, chronic stress, high‑school education level, and possible financial insecurity may limit access to care and adherence to lifestyle recommendations.
risk_factor_summary: Comorbidity flags indicate hypertension, type 2 diabetes, metabolic syndrome, dyslipidemia, and anemia. Cardiovascular risk is high due to age, diabetes, hypertension, obesity, and hypertriglyceridemia, yet no statin therapy is documented. Renal risk is present (diabetes + hypertension) but eGFR and albuminuria data are missing. Metabolic risk includes obesity and hypertriglyceridemia. Hematologic risk from chronic anemia. Psychosocial stressors add to overall complexity. Risk scores are largely unavailable (SBP, DBP, BMI, lipid panel, eGFR).
